newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv sees slower growth in future.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv sees slower growth in future.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment company Autoliv AB managing director Paul Charlety said on Monday that he expected the growth rate in the air bag market to slow down.

"The world market for air bags is expected to grow from about 50 million frontal air bags to about 80 million in the year 2000," Charlety said in a speech at the company's annual general shareholders' meeting.

"Growth will be strongest in Europe, but the growth rate will be the fastest in Japan and the rest of the world. The world market for side air bags is expected to grow from two million last year to about 30 million in the year 2000.
"In summary I can say that we estimate that the market will continue to grow, but that competition will increase and the rate of growth will be slower than it is now," he said.
Charlety said the company would get a few more customers for its side air bags this year. At the moment, Autoliv supplies side air bags to Audi, Volkswagen and Volvo.
